Record which check decided the verdict in a new `entry["verdict_source"]` field, one of `"result" | "spine_terminal" | "blocked_gate" | "none"` (pinned name/values -- do not let the implementer invent its own). Dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer with the completed handoff (this Commander runs headless -- dispatch via `python scripts/run_crew.py --backend external --work-id crew-verdict-and-door --gate g1 --role implementer --handoff .agent-work/crew-verdict-and-door/crew-handoffs/g1-implementer-handoff.md --result .agent-work/crew-verdict-and-door/crew-handoffs/g1-implementer-result.md`, then dispatch the Agent-tool subagent per crew-dispatch.md, then `--verify-result`). g2-implement.title: Task 2 (bounded) -- unbound external-backend door hardening: implement
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate. Cold-critic correction (verified by direct read): ExternalBackend.dispatch (scripts/run_crew.py:1278-1310) builds NO prompt -- its own docstring/comments say the out-of-band caller builds the prompt itself; run_crew.py owns only the registry entry and its own CLI output, so the hardening must land there, not in a 'crew prompt' file this gate cannot reach. Two concrete, both-required, both-achievable pieces: (1) build_entry / ExternalBackend.dispatch records an explicit field on the entry (e.g. `entry["door_bound"] = False` for external-backend dispatches, `True` for cli) so crew-runs.json states the hazard plainly for anyone reading the registry; (2) ExternalBackend.dispatch prints an explicit stderr banner naming the unbound door and instructing the caller to verify spine_status before any mutating verb -- this is what a Commander building an out-of-band prompt actually sees at dispatch time, so it is the practical equivalent of 'in the prompt' without touching any file outside run_crew.py. Binding the door itself out-of-band is impossible by construction (module-import-time env read, pinned by tests/test_mcp_identity.py:914) -- do not attempt it; this gate is about visibility, not binding. Both pieces are in-scope and buildable within scripts/run_crew.py -- if, after this correction, something ELSE still looks like it needs a design decision, name exactly what and stop rather than silently dropping the buildable half.

amendments.reason: This commander's own process is a spine-bound crew (dispatched via run_crew.py --backend cli --spine, per the launch order's own note that Task 2's discipline applies to verifying this run's own door). SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION/SPINE_PARENT are consequently present in this shell's real os.environ -- independently confirmed by running the single test 'clean' (env -u ... unset) and observing it pass, vs. failing when run in this shell as-is. tests/test_mcp_identity.py::DC3InheritanceMechanismTests::test_launching_the_parent_never_touches_the_calling_processs_own_environ asserts these vars are absent from the CALLING process's own environ -- a premise that is false here for a reason unrelated to this gate's change (the vars were inherited from my own dispatch, not leaked by anything run_crew.py does inside this test). Retexting the full-suite check to run in a stripped subshell reproduces the environment the 453f8492 baseline was almost certainly measured in, rather than penalizing this fix for an artifact of my own door binding.
